reviews.text: I checked out LA Dogworks while I was visiting LA for a conference. Brianna was incredibly warm, welcoming and patient. My mini-poodle was only about 5 months and hadn't been to daycare before so I was naturally nervous about introducing him to new dogs in that setting. The facility tour really helped ease my worries. It was clean and thoughtfully designed. They seriously thought of everything from the Zen Den room to the observation area and Fetch Mobile. Andrew, the owner, was also really kind and so great with my puppy. If I lived in LA, this would definitely be my little one's doggie daycare home.
Would give 0 stars if I could. Horrible customer service, incredibly rude!

It’s a great facility with convenient location and hours.

Almost all of the one star reviews are more than five years old
Really care, always getting great feedback from daycare stays. Daycare is 24 hours which is a life saver fory crazy schedule.
They take such good care of my baby!

Where do I even begin? LA Dogworks is hands down the **worst** experience I’ve ever had with a pet service. From the moment I walked in, I knew I’d made a terrible mistake. The staff greeted me with all the warmth of a wet sock—eye-rolls, sighs, and zero interest in answering basic questions about their facilities. If indifference were a crime, this place would be a federal penitentiary.

The “luxury kennel” they advertise? More like a **filthy prison cell**. The floors were sticky, the air reeked of ammonia, and I’m pretty sure I saw a moldy chew toy decaying in the corner. My dog came home reeking of whatever chemical they doused the place with to mask the stench. Oh, and his favorite bed? “Lost.” Because apparently, keeping track of a pet’s belongings is rocket science here.

The grooming service was a **joke**. I requested a simple trim, and my pup returned looking like he’d been attacked by a lawnmower. Uneven patches, a nicked ear (which they “conveniently” forgot to mention), and a suspicious red rash on his belly. When I asked about it, the groomer shrugged and said, “Dogs get stressed.” Thanks for the veterinary bill, guys!

La dogworks is a spotlessly clean facility   & you can tell the people working there care about the dogs. They have a supervised play group area with an employee there at all times . I have visited a dog in boarding there many times & he is well cared for, healthy, & does not appear to be kennel stressed & the staff/owner all know him & treat him kindly.

I have been to quite a few other boarding facilities & have not seen one as nice as ladogworks. The owner definitely takes pride in his facility & cares about animals… it is bright & airy & smells of calming eucalyptus.

It seems that some of the reviews are based on an old reality show & one has to remember these shows are made for entertainment & not real life .
I've always had a great experience with the L.A Dogworks team as well as grooming and non-anesthetic teeth cleaning. My dog loves the play area too!
Great in and out 24hr service. Wonderful staff and my pup is always excited to get in the front door and ready to sleep all the way home when I pick him up!

Edited Review:
I am not sure why it has taken me so long to revise this. I will leave my old review because I think it's only fair to show the good with the bad. This review reflects something that happened years ago, but is the reason why I will never leave my dog in their care again. There was a flu outbreak in the canine community years ago. To the credit of the people who worked here, it was highly advised to vaccinate for flu before bringing in.
I had just gotten Toby vaccinated and thought he would be okay, because he had his own suite and did not play with the other dogs. I left for 4 or 5 days. While visiting family, I got a call that Toby was coughing and needed to be picked up ASAP.
When I got there, my dog had been kept under the cash register in a crate (yep!) for the entire day. He was SEVERELY dehydrated. His fever got up to 104. Though he recovered, his health was never the same. And though there is absolute medical proof of this, I believe it was the catalyst that started his downward spiral in health. He was not the same after that sickness.
Dogs get sick, sometimes, it just can't be helped. But it was made apparent that the owner of the facility was WELL aware of the outbreak (he later hired a vaccination van to come out -  a good thing but very after the fact). If the outbreak was THAT bad, owner of the facility should have shut down - or at least operated at a limited capacity for dogs already there.
My dog certainly NEVER should have been put in a crate under the register. My dog has since passed, I have a new pup - I will not be bringing her to LA Dogworks. Accidents happen, but I cannot be certain that my dog's health will be put above monetary interest.
I give two stars instead of one, because, before this horrible situation, my dog was well treated (as shown in the review below).

Old Review:
I am only giving 4 out of 5 stars (would do 4 1/2 if I could) because it's a bit pricey for me :( However, that being said, I took Toby (my English Bully) to 4 places (all had good reps) before LA Dogworks. At EVERY place Toby would end up injured. This is the only facility I feel safe sending him to. So from that respect, worth the money for him to be happy and healthy. Everyone I have seen there has been incredibly nice, friendly - and washed Toby's belongings if they got dirty (believe, most places wont do that). Lol, changed my mind, giving 'em a 5!
Super friendly staff and great facilities.

I am also here because I watched the profit and it really isn't right that people are reviewing your business based on watching a reality TV show. No I don't agree with the behavior portrayed in the show but this is really unfair. Also if the way you were portrayed wasn't true you wouldn't be responding to each review that have nothing to do with the quality of your business. Praying for you and your employees!
